patch.value: The changelog gate stamps an untagged version with the current date, so its verdict flips every midnight with no commit

Root cause of the test 22 and test 26 failures that blocked pull requests 71, 72 and 73. Two independent causes, both downstream of the npm publish outage. First, the release workflow pushes the release tag only after npm publish succeeds. Publish has been failing since 2026-08-21, so versions 2026.8.22 through 2026.8.24 have release commits on main and no tags. For a version with no tag, pm-changelog synthesises a pending release window and stamps it with the current UTC date rather than anything derived from the input, so changelog check regenerates a different heading date every day and fails on any day after the changelog was generated. Measured directly: with the version set to an untagged 2026.8.20 the generator emits heading 2026.8.20 - 2026-08-24, today's date. The fix is the existing --date-from-version flag, which derives the no-tag fallback from the calendar version itself; verified on pm-ops that an untagged 2026.8.22 then emits 2026-08-22 rather than today. No fleet package passed that flag. Second, the exact devDependency pin on the pm CLI at 2026.8.15 violates pm-changelog 2026.8.17's peer requirement of at least 2026.8.16, so npm ci fails with ERESOLVE before any test runs. Fixed by pinning 2026.8.23 and floating pm-changelog to at least 2026.8.17. Rejected an earlier fix that backfilled the three missing git tags: the release workflow deliberately tags only after a successful publish, so a backfilled tag asserts a release npm never received, and it would have hidden the clock dependence rather than removing it. Those tags were pushed and have been deleted.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Verification, both directions, on this repo with pm-changelog 2026.8.17 installed. Without the flag, an untagged version 2026.8.20 generates the heading 2026.8.20 - 2026-08-24, which is today rather than anything derived from the version. With the flag the version drives the sectioning instead. Cross-checked the same mechanism on pm-ops, where an untagged 2026.8.22 generates 2026-08-22 with the flag and 2026-08-24 without it, which is the decisive comparison because there the version date and today's date differ. Gates after the change: npm test 169 pass 0 fail, coverage 100.00 line 100.00 branch 100.00 funcs with the gate reporting thresholds met, pinned pm health --strict-exit exit 0, changelog:full followed by changelog:check reports up to date.
